description: Loop 10 — Production readiness deep dive. A full audit of the repository against GitHub Actions run history uncovered the single most important fact about this project: of 56 workflow runs across all 9 previous loops, ZERO have succeeded. The iOS app has never compiled in CI, the Android app has never built, and the Supabase and website deploy workflows have never completed. Every previous loop's 'Ship it' verdict was self-assessed from source reading alone, with no green build behind it. This loop closes the real gap between the current state and production: a malformed XcodeGen target spec that fails project generation, Info.plists with no bundle version keys, a watchOS target that imports an iOS-only framework, an Android Gradle wrapper that is a 531-byte shell stub with no wrapper JAR, a settings.gradle.kts typo that fails Gradle configuration, a release build type with no signing config, a development-only APNs entitlement, a missing export-compliance key, and a deprecated Claude model ID in both Edge Functions. Stories are ordered so that the build comes back first and everything else is verified against real CI output rather than asserted.

userStories.title: Fix malformed XcodeGen target spec that fails project generation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `xcodegen generate` to succeed so that CI can build the app at all. The Seddly target in project.yml declares an `info:` block with no `path:` key (XcodeGen's Plist type requires `path`), and nests a `configs:` mapping underneath `info:` where XcodeGen expects it under `settings:`. This is the first step of every CI job and is the prime suspect for the 56 consecutive workflow failures.
acceptanceCriteria: The `info:` block is removed from the Seddly target in project.yml
CFBundleURLTypes with the `seddly` URL scheme is declared directly in Seddly/Resources/Info.plist
Per-configuration CODE_SIGN_STYLE moves from `info.configs` to `settings.configs` on the Seddly target
project.yml parses cleanly against the XcodeGen spec (no unknown or misplaced keys)
The `seddly://` deep link scheme is present in the built Info.plist
CI reaches the build step rather than failing at project generation
userStories.notes: Removed the invalid 'info:' block from the Seddly target — XcodeGen's Plist type requires a 'path:' key, so the block failed spec decoding and would take 'xcodegen generate' down with it. CORRECTION after reading the first real CI log: this was never the observed failure, because the job died two steps earlier at the Docker-based secret scan (see US-189). The spec defect is real and would have surfaced the moment the job got that far, but it was not the cause of the 56-run streak. The 'configs:' mapping nested under 'info:' moved to 'settings.configs' where XcodeGen reads per-configuration overrides, restoring Debug=Automatic / Release=Manual code signing on the app target. CFBundleURLTypes with the seddly scheme moved into Seddly/Resources/Info.plist. Also removed the redundant target-level 'entitlements:' blocks from Seddly and SeddlyWatch: both already set CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS in settings.base, and XcodeGen's 'entitlements' key generates the referenced file, which would have overwritten the checked-in entitlements with an empty plist. Share Extension and Widget already used the settings-only form; all four targets are now consistent.

userStories.title: Add bundle version keys to all four Info.plists
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion in every target's Info.plist. Xcode's Process Info.plist step injects CFBundleIdentifier, CFBundleExecutable, and CFBundleName automatically, but it does NOT inject the version keys unless GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE is on. Today MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION are set in project.yml but never reach any built bundle, so release.yml's `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=${{ github.run_number }}` build-number bump is a no-op and App Store validation rejects the archive.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Resources/Info.plist declares CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)
SeddlyShareExtension/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
SeddlyWidget/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
SeddlyWatch/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
All four bundles therefore carry identical versions, satisfying App Store extension-version matching
Passing CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION on the xcodebuild command line changes the built CFBundleVersion
userStories.notes: Added CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) to all four Info.plists (app, Share Extension, Widget, Watch). Xcode's Process Info.plist step injects CFBundleIdentifier / CFBundleExecutable / CFBundleName automatically but not the version keys — those require GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE, which is off whenever INFOPLIST_FILE names a hand-authored plist. Before this, the MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION set in project.yml reached no bundle, so release.yml's 'CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=${{ github.run_number }}' archive override silently did nothing and App Store validation would reject the archive for missing versions. All four targets resolve the same two variables, so extension versions always match the host app as App Store Connect requires. Verified all four plists parse with plistlib and expose both keys.

userStories.title: Fix watchOS target compilation and packaging
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the SeddlyWatch target to compile and be a valid watchOS app. Three defects block it: (1) Seddly/Sources/Shared/CommitmentLiveActivity.swift imports ActivityKit unconditionally and Shared/ is compiled into the watchOS target, but ActivityKit is not available on watchOS; (2) SeddlyWatch/Info.plist is missing WKApplication, required for a single-target watchOS app; (3) SeddlyWatchComplication.swift declares WidgetKit widgets with no @main WidgetBundle and no widget-extension target, so the complications are dead code.
acceptanceCriteria: ActivityKit usage in Shared/ is guarded by `#if canImport(ActivityKit)` or the file is excluded from the watchOS target
SeddlyWatch/Info.plist declares WKApplication = true
The watch complication is either hosted by a proper watchOS widget-extension target in project.yml, or removed with its intent documented in notes
`xcodebuild -scheme SeddlyWatch` compiles for the watchOS simulator
No duplicate @main declarations exist within any single target
userStories.notes: Three defects fixed. (1) Seddly/Sources/Shared/CommitmentLiveActivity.swift imported ActivityKit unconditionally, and Shared/ is compiled into the watchOS targets — ActivityKit is iOS-only, so every watch build failed at that import. Wrapped the file in '#if canImport(ActivityKit)'; verified no watch code references CommitmentActivityAttributes (only LiveActivityService and CommitmentLiveActivityWidget, both iOS). (2) SeddlyWatch/Info.plist now declares WKApplication=true, required for a single-target watchOS app. (3) SeddlyWatchComplication was a complete, working WidgetKit Widget sitting inside the SeddlyWatch app target with no @main WidgetBundle — WidgetKit only discovers widgets vended by a widget extension's principal bundle, so it compiled but could never be added to a watch face. Moved it to a new SeddlyWatchComplication/ extension target (Info.plist with the widgetkit-extension point, App Group entitlements for SharedModelContainer, new SeddlyWatchComplicationBundle @main), embedded it in the watch app via a target dependency, and registered its provisioning profile in ExportOptions.plist and release.yml. Also registered the seddly-watch:// URL scheme in the Watch Info.plist — WatchLedgerView.onOpenURL already parsed those links and the complication's widgetURL already emitted them, but the scheme was unregistered so complication taps ignored the requested filter. Verified project.yml parses, all seven targets are well-formed, and every shippable bundle ID has exactly one matching provisioning profile.

userStories.title: Replace the stub gradlew with a real Gradle wrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `./gradlew` to actually work. android/gradlew is a hand-written 531-byte shell script whose own comment says 'In production, use the full gradlew from gradle init'; it execs a system `gradle` if present and otherwise exits 1. There is no gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar and no gradlew.bat. Every step of android-ci.yml invokes ./gradlew, so the Android job cannot succeed on a runner without a preinstalled Gradle.
acceptanceCriteria: android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar is present and committed
android/gradlew is the official wrapper script and is executable
android/gradlew.bat is present for Windows developers
gradle-wrapper.properties continues to pin gradle-8.11.1-bin
.gitignore does not exclude the wrapper JAR
`./gradlew --version` succeeds on a machine with no system Gradle installed
userStories.notes: android/gradlew was a hand-written 531-byte shell stub whose own comment read 'In production, use the full gradlew from gradle init' — it exec'd a system gradle if one happened to be installed and otherwise exited 1. There was no gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar and no gradlew.bat. Every step of android-ci.yml invokes ./gradlew, so the Android job could never succeed on a clean runner. Replaced with the official wrapper generated by 'gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.11.1': gradlew (8733 bytes, executable), gradlew.bat (2937 bytes), and gradle-wrapper.jar (43764 bytes). The existing gradle-wrapper.properties turned out to be byte-identical to the generated one, so the 8.11.1-bin pin is unchanged — only the JAR and scripts were missing. Confirmed .gitignore excludes none of the three files (it lists *.apk/*.aab/*.jks/*.keystore but not *.jar). Verified the acceptance criterion directly by running 'env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./gradlew --version' with no system Gradle reachable: the wrapper downloaded the 8.11.1 distribution and reported 'Gradle 8.11.1'.

userStories.title: Fix settings.gradle.kts dependencyResolutionManagement typo
userStories.description: As a developer, I need Gradle configuration to succeed. android/settings.gradle.kts declares a `dependencyResolution { ... }` block, but the Gradle DSL method is `dependencyResolutionManagement`. Gradle fails to resolve the unknown method during settings evaluation, so no Android task can run.
acceptanceCriteria: settings.gradle.kts uses `dependencyResolutionManagement { repositories { ... } }`
repositoriesMode is set explicitly so the project's repositories are authoritative
google() and mavenCentral() remain declared for both pluginManagement and dependency resolution
`./gradlew projects` evaluates settings without an unresolved-method error
userStories.notes: settings.gradle.kts declared 'dependencyResolution { ... }', which is not a Gradle settings DSL method — the correct name is 'dependencyResolutionManagement'. Settings evaluation failed with an unresolved-method error, so no Android task could run at all. Renamed the block and added repositoriesMode = FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS so a build script declaring its own repositories fails loudly instead of silently resolving from an unreviewed source. Verified by running 'gradle projects': the failure moved out of settings evaluation and into plugin resolution, which is as far as this sandbox can go (dl.google.com is blocked by the environment's network policy, so the Android Gradle Plugin cannot be fetched here; GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest has no such restriction).

userStories.title: Add Android release signing configuration
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need `bundleRelease` to produce a signed AAB. android/app/build.gradle.kts has no signingConfigs block at all and the release buildType declares no signingConfig, so the AAB is unsigned and Play Console will reject it. The android-ci.yml release job passes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE / PASSWORD / KEY_ALIAS / KEY_PASSWORD as environment variables that nothing in the build reads, and passes the keystore secret as a path rather than decoding it to a file.
acceptanceCriteria: build.gradle.kts declares a `release` signingConfig sourced from environment variables
The release buildType references that signingConfig
The build degrades gracefully to unsigned when the keystore env vars are absent, so local and PR builds still work
android-ci.yml base64-decodes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 to a keystore file and points the build at that path
No keystore, password, or alias value is committed to the repository
userStories.notes: android/app/build.gradle.kts had no signingConfigs block at all and the release buildType declared no signingConfig, so 'bundleRelease' produced an unsigned AAB that Play Console rejects. Compounding it, android-ci.yml passed ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE straight through as KEYSTORE_FILE — but a GitHub secret holds the keystore's contents, not a path — and nothing in the build read any of the four env vars anyway. Added a release signingConfig sourced from KEYSTORE_FILE / KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / KEY_ALIAS / KEY_PASSWORD, created only when KEYSTORE_FILE is set and the file actually exists. When it is absent the config is not created and the release build stays unsigned but still succeeds, so contributors without the keystore can verify a release build compiles; the build logs a lifecycle warning in that case rather than failing silently. On the CI side, a new step base64-decodes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 into $RUNNER_TEMP (outside the workspace, so it cannot be picked up by the artifact upload) and exports the path via GITHUB_ENV; a verification step greps the AAB's zip index for a META-INF signature block and fails the job if the bundle is unsigned; and an always() step removes the decoded keystore. No keystore, password, or alias value is committed.

userStories.title: Provide the Android lint baseline referenced by the build
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `./gradlew lint` to behave as android-ci.yml documents. build.gradle.kts sets `baseline = file("lint-baseline.xml")` with abortOnError = true, but no lint-baseline.xml exists. Android Gradle Plugin creates the baseline on first run and then fails the build to tell you it did, so the very first CI lint invocation fails by design.
acceptanceCriteria: android/app/lint-baseline.xml exists and is committed, or the baseline reference is removed with rationale in notes
The lint task does not fail purely because the baseline file was absent
abortOnError remains true so newly introduced issues still fail CI
The android-ci.yml comment describing baseline regeneration matches the committed configuration
userStories.notes: build.gradle.kts set 'baseline = file("lint-baseline.xml")' with abortOnError = true, but the file did not exist. When the baseline is missing, AGP creates it and then fails the build to report that it did — so the very first CI lint invocation failed by design, on every run. The in-code comment claiming it was 'auto-generated on first ./gradlew lint run' was true but omitted the failure. Committed android/app/lint-baseline.xml as a valid, deliberately EMPTY baseline (format 6, zero suppressed issues): it hides nothing, so lint still reports everything it finds and abortOnError remains a real gate — it exists solely to remove the bootstrap failure. Corrected the misleading comment and documented that 'gradlew updateLintBaseline' is the way to record genuinely deferred issues. Verified the XML parses and is not gitignored. Could not run lint locally to confirm zero findings because dl.google.com is blocked by this environment's network policy; if CI surfaces pre-existing error-severity issues the right response is to fix them, not to baseline them.

userStories.title: Set aps-environment to production for App Store distribution
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need the app's APNs entitlement to match the distribution channel. Seddly/Resources/Seddly.entitlements declares `aps-environment = development`. An App Store build signed with a development APNs entitlement cannot receive production push notifications, which breaks the Pro+ silent-push sync path that send-silent-push depends on.
acceptanceCriteria: The Release configuration builds with aps-environment = production
Debug builds continue to use the development APNs environment
The split is implemented via per-configuration entitlements files or an xcconfig-driven value, wired in project.yml
ExportOptions.plist and the release workflow remain consistent with the production entitlement
The approach is documented in SETUP.md so the next release engineer does not regress it
userStories.notes: Seddly.entitlements hardcoded 'aps-environment = development'. An App Store build signed with a development APNs entitlement cannot receive production pushes, so the Pro+ silent-push sync driven by the send-silent-push Edge Function would have failed silently in production — the app installs and runs, it just never syncs. Rather than fork the entitlements into two near-identical files that can drift, the value is now $(APS_ENVIRONMENT), resolved from a per-configuration build setting in project.yml (Debug=development, Release=production). Xcode expands build settings in entitlements files during the code-signing step, the same mechanism that resolves $(AppIdentifierPrefix). One file serves both configurations. ExportOptions.plist and release.yml are unaffected because they never referenced the APNs environment. Documented in SETUP.md section 4.6, including why hardcoding a literal back into the file would be a regression.

userStories.title: Declare export-compliance status in Info.plist
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need TestFlight uploads to process without manual intervention. Info.plist does not declare ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, so App Store Connect blocks every build behind a manual export-compliance questionnaire. The app uses only standard HTTPS/TLS and Apple-provided cryptography, which qualifies for the exemption.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Resources/Info.plist declares ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false
A comment records why the exemption applies (HTTPS/TLS and platform cryptography only)
The release workflow uploads to TestFlight without a pending compliance prompt
The claim is consistent with CertificatePinningService and the App Transport Security configuration
userStories.notes: Added ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false to Seddly/Resources/Info.plist. Without the key, App Store Connect holds every build behind a manual export-compliance questionnaire, so the automated TestFlight upload in release.yml would never finish processing without a human answering a form. The exemption is legitimate and consistent with the rest of the app: the only cryptography is standard HTTPS/TLS to Supabase (see the NSAppTransportSecurity block in the same file, which default-denies and pins TLS 1.3 for supabase.co) plus Apple-provided platform cryptography via CertificatePinningService and the Keychain — no proprietary or non-standard encryption ships. Recorded the reasoning inline and in SETUP.md section 4.7, flagging that this is a legal attestation to revisit if custom encryption is ever added.

userStories.title: Migrate Edge Functions off the deprecated Claude Sonnet 4 model
userStories.description: As a backend engineer, I need the Anthropic API calls to target a supported model. Both supabase/functions/extract-commitments/index.ts and generate-dispute-summary/index.ts request `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`. That ID is deprecated with a stated retirement of 2026-06-15, which has passed — requests will 404 and every Pro/Pro+ extraction and dispute summary fails. The migration target is `claude-sonnet-5`. Neither function sets temperature, top_p, top_k, or a thinking budget, so no other request-shape changes are required.
acceptanceCriteria: extract-commitments requests model `claude-sonnet-5`
generate-dispute-summary requests model `claude-sonnet-5`
No sampling parameters (temperature / top_p / top_k) are introduced — they are rejected on this model
No `thinking.budget_tokens` is introduced — it is rejected on this model
anthropic-version stays 2023-06-01 and the raw-HTTP call shape is otherwise unchanged
A comment records the model choice so future migrations are traceable
userStories.notes: Both Edge Functions requested 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'. That ID is deprecated with a stated retirement of 2026-06-15 — already past — so every request would 404 and the entire Pro/Pro+ value proposition (AI extraction and dispute summaries) was dead on arrival. Migrated both to 'claude-sonnet-5', the documented migration target. Verified the migration is clean: neither function sends temperature, top_p, top_k, or a thinking budget, all of which this model rejects with a 400, so no other request-shape change was required. anthropic-version stays 2023-06-01 and the raw-HTTP call shape (correct for a Deno edge runtime with no SDK dependency) is otherwise untouched. Left an inline comment recording the deprecation and the target so the next migration is traceable.

userStories.title: Make SwiftLint pass in CI
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `swiftlint lint --strict` to be a meaningful gate rather than a guaranteed failure. No .swiftlint.yml exists, so SwiftLint runs its full default rule set and --strict promotes every default warning to an error across 120 Swift files. The invocation also lints only Seddly/Sources/, silently excluding the Share Extension, Widget, Watch, and test targets.
acceptanceCriteria: .swiftlint.yml exists at the repository root with an explicit, justified rule configuration
included: covers Seddly/Sources, SeddlyShareExtension, SeddlyWidget, SeddlyWatch and SeddlyTests
excluded: covers generated and build output paths
Rules that conflict with the project's documented conventions are disabled with a comment explaining why
The ci.yml SwiftLint step lints the configured paths rather than a single hardcoded directory
SwiftLint reports zero violations under --strict on the committed source
userStories.notes: There was no .swiftlint.yml at all, so 'swiftlint lint --strict' ran the full default rule set and promoted every default warning to an error across ~14,700 lines of Swift — a guaranteed CI failure once the build got that far. The invocation also passed an explicit 'Seddly/Sources/' path, which overrides a config's included: list, silently skipping the Share Extension, Widget, Watch, complication, and test targets. Added .swiftlint.yml with thresholds derived from measurements of the actual source rather than a template: line_length warns at 200 and errors at 400 (the longest real line is a 370-char escalation-letter template literal; only 14 lines exceed 200), and file_length warns at 800 and errors at 1200 (LedgerView is 1046 lines, CommitmentDetailView 707 — both already decomposed once in Loop 8 under US-153). Disabled seven rules that measure SwiftUI's declarative verbosity rather than code complexity (type_body_length, function_body_length, closure_body_length, cyclomatic_complexity, nesting, trailing_comma, no_grouping_extension), each with the reason stated inline. Relaxed identifier_name's 3-char minimum, which would fire on idiomatic 'id'/'db'/'ok' and SwiftUI generic parameters. Opted into 16 correctness and clarity rules the defaults omit. Scope now covers all seven target directories, verified to exist. IMPORTANT: I could not verify the 'zero violations under --strict' criterion locally — there is no Swift toolchain in this environment and SwiftLint is not installed, so CI is the first place this is actually exercised. Also changed the CI step to fail if the brew install fails, instead of the previous '|| true' which would have let a missing SwiftLint pass silently.

userStories.title: Declare explicit shared schemes for every buildable target
userStories.description: As a CI engineer, I need the schemes referenced by workflows to exist in the generated project. ci.yml runs `xcodebuild -scheme SeddlyWatch`, but only the Seddly target declares a `scheme:` block in project.yml. XcodeGen emits shared schemes only for targets that ask for one, so the watch build step depends on Xcode's scheme autocreation rather than a committed scheme.
acceptanceCriteria: The SeddlyWatch target declares a scheme in project.yml
Every scheme referenced by a workflow file exists in the generated project
`xcodebuild -list -project Seddly.xcodeproj` shows the schemes the workflows invoke
The Seddly scheme keeps its existing test targets, coverage gathering, and StoreKit configuration
userStories.notes: ci.yml runs 'xcodebuild -scheme SeddlyWatch', but only the Seddly target declared a 'scheme:' block in project.yml. XcodeGen emits shared schemes only for targets that ask for one, so the watch build step depended on Xcode's scheme autocreation rather than a scheme committed to the repository — fragile, and invisible to anyone reading project.yml. Added a scheme block to SeddlyWatch (implemented alongside US-171, since a buildable watch target and a usable watch scheme are the same problem). Verified by cross-checking every '-scheme <name>' occurrence across all five workflow files against the targets declaring a scheme in project.yml: both sets are exactly {Seddly, SeddlyWatch}, with nothing referenced-but-undeclared. The Seddly scheme keeps its existing testTargets (SeddlyTests, SeddlyUITests), gatherCoverageData, and storeKitConfiguration. The 'xcodebuild -list' criterion is confirmed transitively by CI: the watch build step invokes the scheme by name and would fail with 'scheme not found' if it were missing.

userStories.title: Pin and harden the Supabase Edge Function lint and type-check steps
userStories.description: As a backend engineer, I need deploy-supabase.yml to type-check the functions it deploys, against a configuration under version control. There is no deno.json, so `deno lint` and `deno check` both ran with unpinned defaults — no strict-mode compiler options, no agreed rule set — and a type error that strict mode would catch could deploy. The `deno check supabase/functions/**/index.ts` invocation also relies on an accident: with globstar off, bash degrades `**` to `*`, so the pattern happens to match the current flat one-directory-per-function layout and would silently stop covering anything nested.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/deno.json exists with explicit lint rules and strict compiler options
Both deno lint and deno check run against that config rather than unpinned defaults
The type-check step enumerates entrypoints explicitly instead of relying on shell glob semantics
The step fails loudly if the expansion does not cover every function directory
All six functions are type-checked, and a type error in any one fails the workflow
Deploy steps still run only after lint and type-check succeed
userStories.notes: Added supabase/functions/deno.json pinning lint rules (recommended tag) and strict compiler options (strict, noImplicitAny, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), and pointed both 'deno lint' and 'deno check' at it — previously both ran with unpinned defaults, so a type error strict mode would catch could deploy. Rewrote the type-check step to enable globstar, expand the entrypoints into an array, and assert the count matches a 'find' of the function directories before invoking deno, so a partial or empty match fails loudly rather than passing as success. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to this story's original premise: I had assumed the '**' glob failed to expand and that deno received a literal pattern. That is wrong — with globstar off bash degrades '**' to '*', and 'supabase/functions/*/index.ts' matches all six functions. Verified directly: the old form expands to exactly the same six paths. So the glob was working, by accident, and would only have broken for a nested layout. The real gap in this story was the missing pinned configuration. The historical Deploy Supabase failures (2026-03-26, 03-27, 04-02) remain unexplained — their logs have aged out with 410 Gone, so I cannot attribute them. Could not execute deno locally to confirm a clean check: deno is not installed in this environment.

Verified by building: 17 pages emitted, all passing the deploy workflow's DOCTYPE and closing-tag validation.

userStories.title: Complete the StoreKit configuration metadata
userStories.description: As a developer testing subscriptions, I need Seddly.storekit to be fully populated. `_applicationInternalID` and `_developerTeamID` are empty strings, and the subscription group ID is the placeholder 21345678, so local StoreKit testing does not mirror the real App Store Connect configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: The StoreKit configuration is documented in SETUP.md with the exact values a developer must fill in from App Store Connect
Placeholder identifiers are clearly marked as placeholders rather than looking like real values
The four product IDs match the identifiers SubscriptionService resolves at runtime
A test asserts the product identifiers used in code match those in the StoreKit configuration
userStories.notes: Seddly.storekit had empty '_applicationInternalID' and '_developerTeamID' and a placeholder subscription group ID (21345678) that read like a real value. More importantly, the four product IDs in Seddly.storekit and the four in AppConstants.SubscriptionProductID were two independent lists with nothing connecting them: renaming a product in one and not the other would surface as a purchase silently failing at runtime, not as a test failure. The pre-existing coverage only asserted the constants contained the substrings 'pro' and 'proplus', which stays true through any rename. Replaced the blank and placeholder identity fields with explicit REPLACE_WITH_ sentinels so a half-configured file is obvious rather than looking like a deliberate blank. Added SeddlyTests/SharedTests/StoreKitConfigurationTests.swift with four Swift Testing cases: every code product ID exists in the configuration; the configuration defines no product the code cannot resolve (catches orphans in both directions); tier-detection substrings are unambiguous, which guards the load-bearing ordering in SubscriptionService where 'contains("proplus")' is checked before 'contains("pro")'; and the identity fields are never silently blank. Wired Seddly.storekit into the SeddlyTests target as a resource in project.yml so the test can load it from its own bundle. Verified statically that both sets are exactly the same four identifiers with no orphans. Documented the fields to fill in, and the parity requirement, in SETUP.md section 9.0. NOT COMPILED: no Swift toolchain here, so the new test file is first built in CI.

userStories.title: Add Play Store publishing and version-code management
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need Android releases to reach the Play Console. The android-ci.yml release job builds an AAB and uploads it as a GitHub artifact, then stops — there is no publishing step. versionCode is hardcoded to 1 in build.gradle.kts, so consecutive releases would collide even if uploaded manually.
acceptanceCriteria: versionCode is derived from the CI run number with a sane local-development fallback
versionName continues to track the marketing version
The release job publishes the signed AAB to a Play Console track using a service-account secret
The publishing step runs only after build, test, and secret-scan jobs succeed
Required repository secrets are documented in SETUP.md
userStories.notes: The release job built an AAB, uploaded it as a GitHub artifact, and stopped — nothing ever reached the Play Console, so shipping required a human to download the artifact and upload it by hand. versionCode was also hardcoded to 1, so two consecutive releases would collide and Play would reject the second even in that manual flow. versionCode now reads ANDROID_VERSION_CODE, which CI sets from github.run_number (monotonic per workflow), falling back to 1 locally — a value that can never reach Play because only the CI release job holds the signing keystore. versionName still tracks the marketing version. Added a Play Console publishing step targeting the internal track with status completed, so the upload is automated while promotion to production stays a deliberate human action. It runs after the existing 'needs: [build-and-test, secrets-scan]' gate and after the US-174 signature verification, so an unsigned or unverified bundle can never be published. Documented all five Android secrets in SETUP.md section 12 — they were consumed by android-ci.yml but had never been documented at all — plus the watch complication profile from US-171, and flagged the ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE to ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 rename for anyone migrating. Verified by diffing every 'secrets.*' reference across all five workflow files against the documented names: nothing is used-but-undocumented.

userStories.title: Make CI actually run on feature-branch pushes
userStories.description: As a developer, I need CI to run when I push to a feature branch. ci.yml declares `push: branches: ['*']`, but a single asterisk in a GitHub Actions branch filter matches only branch names containing no slash. Every branch this project uses is named `claude/<something>`, so no push to a feature branch has ever triggered CI — confirmed against the run history, where every feature-branch run was a `pull_request` event and every `push` event was on main. Developers get zero build feedback until they open a pull request, which is a large part of why 56 consecutive failures went unnoticed.
acceptanceCriteria: ci.yml uses a branch pattern that matches slash-containing branch names
Pushing to a claude/* branch triggers the CI workflow
The existing pull_request trigger against main is preserved
Concurrency grouping still cancels superseded runs for the same ref
A run appears for this branch on the next push, confirming the fix end to end
userStories.notes: ci.yml declared "push: branches: ['*']". A single asterisk in a GitHub Actions branch filter does not match a slash, so pushes to this project's claude/<name> branches never triggered CI. Confirmed against the run history: every feature-branch run was a pull_request event and every push event was on main — meaning developers got zero build feedback until opening a PR, a large part of why 56 consecutive failures went unnoticed across nine loops. Changed to '**', which matches slashes. The pull_request trigger against main and the cancel-in-progress concurrency group keyed on github.ref are both unchanged.

userStories.title: Run the secret scan on Linux instead of the macOS build job
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the iOS CI job to reach the build. The 'Scan for secrets' step used trufflesecurity/trufflehog, a Docker action, inside a job running on macos-15 — and GitHub's macOS runners ship no Docker daemon. The first live log captured for this project shows the step failing with 'docker: command not found' and exit 127, twelve seconds into the run, at step 2 — before Xcode selection, before xcodegen, before any compilation. This is the actual root cause of the 56-run failure streak: no iOS job has ever reached a compiler. android-ci.yml already runs its scan as a separate ubuntu-latest job; ci.yml should match.
acceptanceCriteria: Secret scanning runs in its own job on ubuntu-latest, where Docker is available
The macOS build job no longer contains a Docker-based step
A verified-secret finding still fails the workflow
The build job proceeds past the point where the scan used to abort it
The layout matches the secrets-scan job already present in android-ci.yml
userStories.notes: Root cause of the 56-run failure streak, found by reading the first live CI log this project has ever produced. ci.yml ran 'Scan for secrets' via trufflesecurity/trufflehog — a Docker action — as step 2 of a job on macos-15. GitHub's macOS runners ship no Docker daemon, so the step failed with 'docker: command not found' and exit 127 twelve seconds into the run, before Xcode selection, before xcodegen, before a single file was compiled. No iOS CI job has ever reached a compiler. Moved secret scanning into its own ubuntu-latest job, matching the layout android-ci.yml already used, so the macOS job now proceeds to the build. Also dropped the redundant '--fail' from extra_args: the action's own invocation already passes --fail, so a verified finding still fails the workflow.

userStories.title: Materialize Release.xcconfig in the CI build job
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `xcodegen generate` to succeed in the CI build job. project.yml declares configFiles for both Debug and Release, and XcodeGen validates every referenced file when it loads the spec — regardless of which configuration is being built. ci.yml materialized only Debug.xcconfig from its sample; Release.xcconfig is gitignored and was never created, so generation aborted with 'Spec validation error: Invalid config file "Seddly/Config/Release.xcconfig" for config "Release"'. Found in the first CI run that ever reached the xcodegen step, after US-189 removed the Docker blocker.
acceptanceCriteria: ci.yml materializes both Debug.xcconfig and Release.xcconfig from their committed samples
xcodegen generate completes without a spec validation error
Only placeholder credentials are used — AppConfiguration treats REPLACE_ values as absent
release.yml continues to write the real Release.xcconfig from GitHub secrets
No real credential is committed or written by the CI build job
userStories.notes: project.yml declares configFiles for both Debug and Release, and XcodeGen validates every referenced config file at spec-load time no matter which configuration is being built. ci.yml copied only Debug.xcconfig.sample, and Release.xcconfig is gitignored, so 'xcodegen generate' aborted with 'Spec validation error: Invalid config file "Seddly/Config/Release.xcconfig" for config "Release"'. Now copies both samples. Safe: Release.xcconfig.sample carries REPLACE_WITH_CI_SECRET placeholders, which AppConfiguration.isPlaceholder catches via its 'REPLACE_' check and resolves to nil, and it #includes the committed Shared.xcconfig so it is self-sufficient. release.yml still writes the real Release.xcconfig from GitHub secrets and is unaffected. Found by reading the first CI run in this project's history that reached the xcodegen step at all.

userStories.title: Fix the Astro build failure that has blocked every website deploy
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `astro build` to succeed. src/pages/c/[id].astro is a dynamic route with no getStaticPaths(), which a static Astro build requires, so the build failed with GetStaticPathsRequired and the website has never deployed — the third pipeline in this project that has never once succeeded. Enumerating the paths is impossible by nature: these are share links keyed by commitment UUID, created by users long after the site is built.
acceptanceCriteria: astro build completes and emits every page
/c/<id> share links still resolve and still offer the seddly://c/<id> deep link
The commitment id is read at runtime and validated before use
A crafted path cannot inject markup or a foreign scheme into the deep link
The build output passes the deploy workflow's HTML validation
userStories.notes: src/pages/c/[id].astro was a dynamic route with no getStaticPaths(), which a static Astro build requires — 'astro build' failed with GetStaticPathsRequired, so the website has never deployed. Confirmed pre-existing by stashing my changes and rebuilding. Enumerating paths is impossible here: /c/<id> links are keyed by commitment UUID and created by users long after the site is built. Converted the route to a single static shell at src/pages/c/index.astro that reads the id from window.location.pathname at runtime, and added public/_redirects with '/c/*  /c/index.html  200' — a Cloudflare Pages rewrite, not a redirect, so the visitor's URL stays /c/<id> and the link remains shareable. The id is validated against /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$/ before being written into the DOM or the seddly:// href, and set via textContent and setAttribute rather than innerHTML. Verified with 8 cases including path traversal (/c/../../etc), encoded markup (/c/%3Cscript%3E), attribute-breakout (/c/a%22onload%3D1), and an over-length id — all rejected. Also replaced the hardcoded placeholder App Store URL (id0000000000) on that page with /download. Build now emits 17 pages and passes the deploy workflow's DOCTYPE and closing-tag validation.

userStories.title: Resolve simulator destinations at runtime instead of hardcoding device names
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the build steps to target a simulator that actually exists on the runner. ci.yml hardcoded 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16,OS=latest' and 'name=Apple Watch Series 10 (46mm)'. Runner images rotate which simulator runtimes are preinstalled, and the current macos-15 image reported no iOS runtime at all — the only eligible destination was the 'Any iOS Device' placeholder, with 'iOS 18.4 is not installed'. xcodebuild exited 70 with 'Unable to find a destination matching the provided destination specifier'. Found in the first CI run that ever got past project generation.
acceptanceCriteria: No workflow step hardcodes a simulator device name or OS version
An available iOS and watchOS simulator is discovered at runtime and referenced by UDID
If the image ships without a runtime, the platform is downloaded rather than failing
The job fails with a clear message if no simulator can be obtained even after download
The resolved UDIDs are logged so a destination problem is diagnosable from the run output
userStories.notes: ci.yml hardcoded 'name=iPhone 16' and 'name=Apple Watch Series 10 (46mm)'. The macos-15 image reported no iOS simulator runtime at all — the only eligible destination was the 'Any iOS Device' placeholder with 'iOS 18.4 is not installed' — so xcodebuild exited 70 with 'Unable to find a destination matching the provided destination specifier'. Replaced with a 'Resolve simulator destinations' step that parses 'xcrun simctl list devices available -j', sorts by runtime identifier so the newest runtime wins, and exports one UDID per platform to GITHUB_ENV; the three build/test steps then use -destination "id=$IOS_SIM" / "id=$WATCH_SIM". If no runtime is present the step runs 'xcodebuild -downloadPlatform' and re-resolves, and fails with an explicit ::error:: if still empty. Resolved UDIDs are echoed for diagnosability. Verified locally: extracted the exact PICK expression back out of the committed YAML and ran it against sample simctl JSON — it selects the iOS-18-4 device over iOS-18-2, selects the watchOS device, ignores isAvailable:false entries, and returns empty (triggering the download branch) for an empty device set. An earlier draft used a multi-line embedded heredoc that broke the YAML block scalar; caught by parsing the file and rewritten as single-line invocations.
